text: We were somewhere outside the city limits when the whole rotten enterprise began to come apart at the seams. The speedometer said ninety and the gas gauge said empty and my so-called attorney was screaming about bats again, great flapping things the size of garbage-can lids, none of which existed except in the swampy back rooms of his fevered skull. Keep driving, I told him. We can't stop here. This is bat country and the night is young and mean and full of teeth.

The American Dream, as near as I could tell from the front seat of a rented convertible doing ninety through the desert at four in the morning, was mostly a matter of nerve and bad chemicals and a willingness to keep your foot down long after any sane man would have pulled over and wept. Nobody pulled over. That was the whole sick genius of the thing. We just kept going, faster and louder, on the theory that if you went fast enough the wheels would never quite touch the ground.

By dawn the suite looked like the aftermath of a small, stupid war — bottles everywhere, a television set face-down in the bathtub, and somewhere under the wreckage a telephone ringing with the grim persistence of a creditor or a cop. I let it ring. There are mornings when answering the phone is the single dumbest move a man can make, and this was shaping up to be the worst of them. My head felt like a parking garage. The sun came up like an accusation.

Politics in this country is a low business, a greasy carnival run by swine in good suits, and anybody who tells you otherwise is either selling something or running for office, which amounts to the same filthy thing. I have watched these creatures up close, close enough to smell the fear-sweat under the cologne, and I am here to report that the rot goes all the way down. All the way. There is no bottom to it. You could dig for a hundred years and never hit clean dirt.

We hit the strip at midnight with the radio howling and a trunk full of supplies that would have put a respectable pharmacist in prison for the rest of his natural life. The lights came up out of the dark like the gates of some electric hell built specifically to separate fools from their money, and we drove straight into the heart of it, laughing, because what else can you do? You can't run. You can't hide. You can only put your foot down and aim for the bright spot and hope the brakes hold.
